solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cab is pretty damned fine, as they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: very good-looking, pronounced the same as the cab

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a taxi, declaring it rather splendid in a colloquial phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent D in 'handsome' is what makes the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the Victorian forerunner of the taxi.

clue.text: Point of short pause on November feast for soldier

parts.note: the punctuation mark that marks a brief break
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A brief break in a November banquet, laid on for a serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the comma before the rest, reading down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids, a specific kind of fighting man.

clue.text: Hum and haw over dismissals for carriers

parts.note: to haver is to dither or talk hesitantly
getting the sack means being fired

explanation.surface: A manager dithering over who to fire, with the delivery staff in the firing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriers' reads as delivery people but means bags; 'over' places the first piece above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Haversacks are bags slung over the shoulder for carrying things, so they are carriers.

clue.text: Spacious cowshed where days are wasted

indicators.note: things wasted are lost and gone, so that letter drops out of the word

parts.note: the farm building where cows are milked
D is the standard abbreviation for day or days

explanation.surface: A roomy cattle shed where farmhands idle their days away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is the hinge: the cowshed is the place from which the days vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is open and well ventilated, so roomy and light: a close synonym.

clue.text: Unexpected pain concerning plant

parts.note: as in a snap election or snap decision, one called without warning
a drag is a nuisance or bore
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A sudden twinge to do with some greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected pain' looks like an anagram of pain, but the clue is a plain three-part charade.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: Lots of trousers

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a big pile of trousers; 'of' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means a large amount, and it is also slang for wide-legged trousers.

clue.text: Bravo! Workers' association is swelling

parts.note: B is Bravo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a trade union represents workers

explanation.surface: Applause for a labour movement that is growing in strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bravo!' reads as a cheer and 'swelling' as growing membership, but they are a letter and a foot complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunion is a painful bony swelling on the joint of the big toe.

clue.text: Member of the clergy always plugging split

indicators.note: a plug fills a gap, so one word goes inside the other to stop it up

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
ever means at all times, as in ever ready

explanation.surface: A priest forever papering over a schism in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is used as a noun for a minister or priest, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Praise a daughter facing speech

parts.note: taken as written
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
a formal address

explanation.surface: Commending one's daughter as she stands up to give a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worship or reverent admiration, which is praise in its strongest form.

clue.text: Entertain a girl such as Clio

parts.note: taken as written
Clio, Muse of history, is one of the nine daughters of Zeus who inspire the arts

explanation.surface: Keeping a young woman called Clio amused.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio looks like any girl's name; the classical Muse is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to divert or delight them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Review, we hear, of warm weather

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a review is a recap or summing-up

explanation.surface: A report, rumour has it, about the hot spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Summery describes things typical of summer, the season of warm weather.

clue.text: I am in to absolutely smash hobby

indicators.note: in places one word inside another, here within the verb that follows

parts.note: to paste someone is to beat or thrash them soundly
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they are up for smashing a hobby out of the park.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is an activity done to pass time pleasantly, the same as a leisure interest.

clue.text: Motorway on the west of an isle

parts.note: M is used for British motorways, as in the M1
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorway running along the western side of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry west is the left, so the motorway letter comes first. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is the island in the Irish Sea, known as the Isle of Man, a self-governing Crown dependency.

clue.text: Conventional Scandinavian taking in clubs for folk do?

parts.note: square means old-fashioned and conventional

indicators.note: taking something in means admitting it inside, so one letter sits within the word

parts.note: a person from Denmark
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A straight-laced Scandinavian bringing golf clubs along to a folk gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a folk do is a social gathering for country dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A square dance is a folk dance for four couples arranged in a square, and the event where it is danced.

clue.text: Pimping up blue Austin would be improper

indicators.note: pimping up a car means customising it heavily, so the letters are remodelled

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Customising a blue Austin car with flashy extras would be in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin is a classic British car make, which is why 'pimping up' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable means inappropriate or unfitting, a close synonym of improper.

clue.text: Share senior copper's commendation

parts.note: a Detective Inspector, a senior police officer
the possessive ending taken as written
a tribute is an expression of praise

explanation.surface: Passing round a high-ranking police officer's citation for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: A copper is a British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To share something out is to distribute it, dividing it among people.

clue.text: With stiff upper lip son stands by restorative with no note

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: with none of something means it is left out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a tonic is a pick-me-up
N is a standard abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A son bravely sticks with a pick-me-up while refusing to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without showing feeling; used adjectivally it means uncomplaining, like keeping a stiff upper lip.

clue.text: Cancel drink with journos in general

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
the press is journalists taken collectively

explanation.surface: Calling off a drinks session with the reporters at large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' signals journalists as a body rather than individuals; journo is slang for journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress something, such as a report, is to stop or quash it, effectively cancelling it.

clue.text: Flag source of power in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going back the way you came, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: gas is a fuel used to generate power

explanation.surface: A banner from the power station, carried by an army falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' wants to be a banner; it is the verb meaning to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to droop or lose energy, and to sag is to sink or weaken in the same way.

clue.text: Fragment is distributed, no need for answer

indicators.note: what is not needed can be dispensed with, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: divided out among people
A is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A broken piece is handed round with nobody required to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small torn strip or scrap, which is a fragment.

clue.text: Taking turns train got derailed

indicators.note: a derailed train is knocked out of line, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A train that came off the rails while taking the bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking turns' suggests a train cornering; it means alternating.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating can mean alternating in turn, as staff rotating through shifts take turns.

clue.text: Trojan prince worked iron — he is a community member

parts.note: the son of King Priam whose abduction of Helen began the Trojan War

indicators.note: worked metal is beaten into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A mythical prince turned blacksmith settles into local life.
explanation.definitionFit: A parishioner is someone who belongs to a parish, the local church community.

clue.text: Gym in actual cancellation

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the word that follows

parts.note: actual means genuine
physical education, the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: A real gym session being called off.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeal is the revoking of a law, which is a formal cancellation.

clue.text: Char cheers packing energy

indicators.note: packing something means stowing it inside, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady saying thanks while bursting with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a cleaning woman, but here it is the British slang word for a cuppa; 'cheers' means thanks, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is old British slang, from Chinese cha, for tea the drink.

clue.text: Snap, a British game with point

parts.note: taken as written
B is an abbreviation for British
RU is rugby union
PT is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Snap, the card game, described as a British game with a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap reads as the card game; it is the adjective, as in a snap decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap decision is sudden and hasty, so snap as an adjective means abrupt.

clue.text: Imitation parcel I must move

indicators.note: if things must move they are shifted from their places, so the letters change positions

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A counterfeit package that a courier has to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy of something, an imitation of the original.

clue.text: One had them — same in Latin

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
had contracts to 'd, as in I'd
them is clipped to 'em in casual speech

explanation.surface: Somebody owned them once, which is the same thing, said in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The contractions are read the way they are spoken: I'd and 'em.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is the Latin word for 'the same', used in citations to refer back to an author already named.

clue.text: Mafioso, say, is a brute born for term in prison

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: a monster is a cruel, savage person
B is the abbreviation for born
surface padding that loosely points at the letter swapped out, the n being a mathematical term

explanation.surface: A gangster described as a thug, born to serve time behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter replaced is the N, apparently the 'term' (as in the nth term of a series) sitting in the brute, though the phrase is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A mafioso is a member of the Mafia, one example of a gangster, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Succeeded dropping down in complacent fools

indicators.note: in a down entry, a letter dropping down leaves its place at the top and falls to the bottom

parts.note: self-satisfied
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Success brings a comedown for self-satisfied idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is British slang for a gullible person, a dupe or fool.

clue.text: Small lie is off

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a tale is a fib, as in telling tales

explanation.surface: A white lie is no longer acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' reads as cancelled; 'off' alone is the definition, as food goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is off has gone bad, and stale food is no longer fresh.

clue.text: Take it easy! Sort of dash in to become happy

indicators.note: in places the piece before it inside the phrase that comes after

parts.note: a face lights up with joy
an en dash is a punctuation mark the width of the letter N

explanation.surface: Telling someone to relax: a quick dash inside will cheer them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of dash' suggests rushing; it is the typographer's en dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighten up is an idiomatic command telling someone to relax and stop being so serious.
